cycle.objective: Fill explicit Tim Hortons technology-stack and franchise-disclosure gaps, then complete the bounded enterprise profile across identity, ownership, footprint, leadership, strategy, financial/operating health, technology lifecycle, franchise governance, and dated change signals.

budget.description: Complete current profile across required modules.

questions: Which restaurant-technology products and vendors are currently selected, piloted, rolling out, or live, at what scope?
What do current public franchise disclosures say about required technology, approved vendors, fees, replacement obligations, and governance?
Who owns and leads Tim Hortons today?
What is the current restaurant footprint and recent operating performance?
What material 2026 strategy and restaurant-investment signals affect technology buying or deployment?

findings.claim: Tim Hortons is an RBI-owned QSR brand founded in 1964 and remains the largest coffee-and-baked-goods restaurant chain in Canada by restaurant count.
findings.commercial_relevance: Confirms parent-level buying context under Restaurant Brands International.

findings.claim: RBI reported 6,209 Tim Hortons restaurants globally as of June 30, 2026.
findings.commercial_relevance: Establishes enterprise scale; the RBB prior-state unit count of 653 is U.S.-oriented and should not be substituted for global footprint.
findings.limitations: The 10-Q global count includes restaurants outside the Tim Hortons Canada/U.S. reporting segment.

findings.claim: Axel Schwan remains President, Tim Hortons Canada & U.S.
findings.commercial_relevance: Confirms current top brand executive for Canada/U.S. operating and franchise priorities.

findings.claim: For the Tim Hortons Canada/U.S. segment in Q2 2026, system-wide sales were approximately US$2.003 billion, system-wide sales growth was 0.4%, comparable sales were 0.1%, and Canada comparable sales were 0.1%. The segment ended the quarter with 4,570 restaurants, up from 4,521 a year earlier.
findings.commercial_relevance: Shows footprint growth but sharply slower same-store momentum in Q2, increasing emphasis on operational efficiency, traffic and digital value.
findings.limitations: Segment metrics exclude international Tim Hortons activity, which is reported in RBI's INTL segment.

findings.claim: Tim Hortons' 2026 Canadian strategy includes further menu innovation, digital value through Tims Rewards, guest-experience improvement, more kiosks, restaurant renovations and equipment upgrades.
findings.commercial_relevance: Creates active deployment windows across front-of-house digital, kitchen equipment and restaurant refresh programs.
findings.limitations: Canada-specific strategy should not automatically be applied to U.S. or international franchise systems.

findings.claim: The Tims app, Tims Rewards, mobile ordering and Scan & Pay are live first-party guest technologies. Scan & Pay is available at participating restaurants in both Canada and the U.S. and combines payment, points earning and reward redemption in one QR-code scan.
findings.commercial_relevance: Confirms a mature first-party digital/loyalty/payment experience that any POS or payments displacement must integrate with.
findings.limitations: The public sources do not identify the underlying third-party loyalty or payment-orchestration software provider, if any.

findings.claim: Tim Hortons reported more than 800 digital kiosks installed in Canadian restaurants by February 2026, with more planned.
findings.commercial_relevance: Confirms a material self-service footprint and continued rollout rather than a limited pilot.
findings.limitations: The kiosk hardware/software vendor is not named in the first-party source.

findings.claim: Panasonic/Quick Service Technologies maintains a current Tim Hortons-specific POS support workflow. The current ownership-change form requires Panasonic assistance and includes Chase merchant/terminal identifiers, Moneris ECR numbers and kiosk terminal IDs.
findings.commercial_relevance: Strong evidence that Panasonic/QST remains materially embedded in Tim Hortons restaurant POS/support infrastructure.
findings.limitations: The public support portal does not disclose total installed location count or prove a single systemwide POS SKU across every geography.

findings.claim: CLEARVIEW currently identifies Tim Hortons USA and Tim Hortons Canada users/customers, and its platform covers restaurant back-office functions including purchasing, forecasting, labor/workforce scheduling and operational analytics.
findings.commercial_relevance: Establishes a current back-office/workforce/inventory incumbent relationship that overlaps Genius Back Office and adjacent capabilities.
findings.limitations: Vendor pages do not state chainwide penetration or whether deployment is mandated versus franchisee-selected.

findings.claim: i3 International currently markets its Velocity drive-thru timing/video analytics solution with Tim Hortons customer evidence, including a Tim Hortons franchisee testimonial.
findings.commercial_relevance: Shows franchisee-level adoption of drive-thru/video analytics but not a brandwide standard.
findings.limitations: Vendor marketing and testimonial evidence only; systemwide deployment is not established.

findings.claim: Solink and StarPOS actively market a Tim Hortons-specific video/POS integration workflow, indicating another franchisee-level security/loss-prevention technology path.
findings.commercial_relevance: Suggests POS/video integration requirements and non-uniform franchisee technology choices.
findings.limitations: Does not establish corporate selection, approved-vendor status or chainwide scope.

findings.claim: Tim Hortons USA Inc. holds an active Wisconsin franchise registration expiring March 13, 2027.
findings.commercial_relevance: Confirms a current 2026 franchise disclosure cycle is in force.
findings.limitations: The regulator index confirms registration but did not expose the underlying PDF through this research interface.

findings.claim: Current 2026 FDD-derived public sources report recurring Restaurant Technology charges of approximately $450-$1,400 per month and ongoing technology support including POS, TimZone and Tim Card.
findings.commercial_relevance: Technology is a direct recurring franchisee cost center, material to replacement ROI and total cost of ownership.
findings.limitations: Underlying full 2026 FDD was not freely retrievable; value comes from a current FDD-derived public summary.

findings.claim: The 2026 franchise disclosure framework uses an approved-supplier model covering equipment, POS systems, ordering systems and customer communication systems. The franchisor may designate itself, an affiliate or a third party as sole supplier for an item and may charge the franchisee or proposed supplier for evaluation of alternatives.
findings.commercial_relevance: Technology procurement is governed at the franchisor/approved-supplier layer; a franchisee cannot freely substitute core systems.
findings.limitations: FranCloud appears to index a development-agreement filing variant with a small outlet count; requirement language is used, but its unit counts are not generalized to the full U.S. estate.

findings.claim: Current 2026 FDD-derived Item 22 language requires prescribed POS and polling/data-collection systems and permits Tim Hortons USA to access restaurant-system data. This establishes corporate governance over POS/data architecture even where a specific named POS vendor is not publicly mandated.
findings.commercial_relevance: Any POS replacement must satisfy franchisor-prescribed data, polling and interoperability requirements.
findings.limitations: The underlying filing text is exposed through a secondary FDD-derived interface; exact applicability by agreement type must be preserved.

findings.claim: Current 2026 FDD-derived sources report refurbishment obligations of up to $250,000 and give the franchisor broad control over approved technology systems and suppliers; however, the exact current contractual wording for mandatory hardware/software replacement timing was not independently recovered from the full 2026 FDD.
findings.commercial_relevance: Replacement obligations exist at the broader refurb/system-governance level, but precise technology refresh cadence remains a follow-up gap.
findings.limitations: Do not convert the older historical Tim Hortons replacement language into a 2026 contractual fact without the current full FDD.

findings.claim: FDD-derived public evidence names First Data by Fiserv in the 2026 filing, but the available evidence does not establish it as a mandatory current payment processor. Separately, Panasonic's current Tim Hortons support form accommodates Chase and Moneris identifiers.
findings.commercial_relevance: Payment processing should be treated as a mixed/approved ecosystem rather than a single proven global incumbent.
findings.limitations: The role of Fiserv versus Chase/Moneris varies by agreement, geography, processor/acquirer role and restaurant configuration.

findings.claim: Tim Hortons and Canadian restaurant owners committed approximately C$400 million in 2026 to build 80 new Canadian restaurants and renovate 400 existing restaurants, including improvements for digital ordering/pickup and upgraded kitchen equipment.
findings.commercial_relevance: Creates a large active refresh window where POS, kiosks, DMB, kitchen, network and payment hardware could be touched.
findings.limitations: Specific technology vendors for the 2026 renovation program are not named.

findings.claim: A current RBI job posting for Tim Hortons U.S. explicitly includes POS management, launch testing, and oversight of the POS relationship with the Canadian technology team and POS vendor.
findings.commercial_relevance: Confirms an active centralized POS vendor relationship and cross-border governance even though the vendor is not named publicly.
findings.limitations: Job description does not identify the incumbent POS vendor or installed product.

gap_outcomes.outcome: Current public evidence establishes: (1) first-party Tims app/Tims Rewards/mobile ordering/Scan & Pay live in Canada and U.S.; (2) 800+ self-order kiosks installed in Canada with continued rollout; (3) a current Panasonic/Quick Service Technologies Tim Hortons POS support relationship with Chase/Moneris/kiosk configuration fields; (4) current CLEARVIEW back-office customer evidence for Tim Hortons USA and Canada; and (5) franchisee-level i3 drive-thru/video analytics and Solink/StarPOS security/POS integrations. The exact systemwide POS SKU/vendor mandate, kiosk vendor, KDS vendor, digital-menu-board vendor and global payment processor remain unresolved and are not guessed.
remaining_subgaps: Exact current systemwide POS software SKU and installed-location scope
Digital menu board CMS/hardware vendor and scope
Payment processor/acquirer roles by Canada vs U.S. and franchise agreement type

gap_outcomes.outcome: A current 2026 franchise disclosure cycle is verified via Wisconsin DFI. FDD-derived public sources support an approved-supplier model for POS, ordering and customer-communication systems; franchisor authority to prescribe POS/data-collection systems and access restaurant data; recurring Restaurant Technology charges of approximately $450-$1,400/month; supplier-evaluation cost recovery; and refurbishment obligations up to $250,000. The exact current contractual technology-replacement cadence and a definitive list of mandated named technology vendors could not be verified from a freely accessible underlying 2026 FDD PDF, so those points remain explicitly partial.
remaining_subgaps: Exact 2026 hardware/software replacement language and cadence
Current official approved-vendor list by technology category
Whether First Data/Fiserv is mandatory, optional, legacy or agreement-specific
Whether the development-agreement technology clauses differ materially from standard-shop franchise agreement clauses

conflicts.analysis: FDD Exchange summarizes the primary U.S. franchise offer at 693 outlets at 2025 year-end, while FranCloud displays an eight-unit filing context with materially different economics and development-agreement language. These appear to be different offering/agreement variants rather than true system-count disagreement. The packet uses FDD Exchange for main U.S. scale and FranCloud only for requirement language explicitly framed as developer/franchise agreement evidence.

FDD-derived evidence names First Data/Fiserv without proving mandate; Panasonic's current Tim Hortons support workflow includes Chase and Moneris identifiers. This is best represented as a multi-provider/role-specific ecosystem until contract scope is independently resolved.

conflicts.topic: RBB prior scale vs current global scale
conflicts.analysis: The RBB prior state records 653 units, which aligns with a U.S.-specific estate, while RBI reports 6,209 Tim Hortons restaurants globally and 4,570 in the Canada/U.S. TH reporting segment. These are different scopes, not a factual contradiction.

unanswered_questions: What exact POS software and hardware SKUs are currently mandated or approved in Canada and the U.S., and what percentage of restaurants run each?
Who supplies the 800+ Tim Hortons kiosks in Canada, and what is the rollout target?
What KDS and digital menu board platforms are current standards?
What are the precise current processor/acquirer/gateway roles of Fiserv/First Data, Chase and Moneris by country and agreement type?
What does the full 2026 FDD say verbatim about hardware/software replacement obligations, upgrade cadence and franchisor authority to impose replacement?
Is CLEARVIEW mandatory, preferred, or optional at franchisee level, and what is its active store count?

method_feedback.productive_patterns: Primary SEC/RBI/Tim Hortons sources were strongest for ownership, footprint, performance, leadership and rollout scope. Current vendor support portals were unusually productive for identifying real restaurant technology relationships where marketing case studies were too generic. FDD-derived public summaries were necessary because the regulator index confirmed the filing but the underlying 2026 PDF was not freely retrievable through this environment.
method_feedback.unproductive_patterns: Generic searches for Oracle, Olo, Punchh, Paytronix, Brink, Xenial and other common restaurant vendors did not produce current primary evidence strong enough to assign them as Tim Hortons incumbents. Historical vendor references were not promoted to current facts.
method_feedback.proposed_method_changes: For Tim Hortons, future cycles should prioritize Panasonic/QST support artifacts, state-regulator FDD attachments where directly downloadable, RBI job postings that name technology responsibilities, and franchisee-specific evidence to resolve scope. Separate Canada, U.S. and international stacks rather than assuming one global architecture.
method_feedback.next_cycle_recommendations: Obtain the full current 2026 FDD directly from a free state regulator attachment if available; map POS/kiosk/KDS/DMB/payment vendors by geography; validate CLEARVIEW installed count; identify technology owner(s) beneath Axel Schwan and the Canadian technology team.

commercial_assessment.buying_model: Franchisor-governed core standards with franchisee execution and some franchisee-level technology variation.
commercial_assessment.technology_posture: Active modernization rather than wholesale stack replacement: digital kiosks, app/loyalty/payment integration, restaurant renovations and equipment refresh coexist with an entrenched Panasonic/QST and CLEARVIEW ecosystem.
commercial_assessment.opportunity_implication: Best approach is category-by-category displacement or payments-funded modernization tied to 2026 refresh cycles, not an assumption that Tim Hortons will replace its entire restaurant stack at once.
